title: Multimodal Homogeneity: Do Vision-Language Models Converge on Image Descriptions?

original_idea.title: Multimodal Homogeneity: Do Vision-Language Models Converge on Image Descriptions?
original_idea.problem: The Artificial Hivemind effect has only been documented for text-only models. It is unknown whether multimodal models show the same convergence on image captioning and visual question answering.
original_idea.direction: Adapt the pairwise similarity methodology to image description tasks: feed the same set of 500+ images to 5+ VLMs and measure inter-model semantic similarity of generated descriptions.
original_idea.why_it_matters: VLMs are deployed in high-stakes visual domains (medical imaging, surveillance, accessibility tools); homogeneous visual interpretation creates correlated failure risk.
original_idea.relevant_context: Chain of Attack (CVPR 2025) shows adversarial transferability across multimodal models; Artificial Hivemind documents the effect in text only.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: extending to VLMs is interesting and relevant to high-stakes visual domains, but the safety impact chain is less direct than text-based safety tasks.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: working with multiple VLMs, managing image datasets, and handling multimodal API calls requires more infrastructure and expertise than beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: running 5+ VLMs on 500+ images and computing similarity is substantial in terms of compute, API cost, and data management.

novelty.reasoning: No existing study applies the Artificial Hivemind pairwise similarity methodology to VLM image descriptions. Chain of Attack shows adversarial transferability across VLMs but does not measure semantic homogeneity of normal outputs. This is a genuinely unexplored extension.

evidence.finding: Documents the hivemind effect in text-only models but does not extend to multimodal settings.
Demonstrates adversarial transferability across VLMs (GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini), suggesting shared representations, but does not measure output homogeneity directly.
Different VLMs prioritize different attributes (size vs habitat of objects), suggesting some heterogeneity in representations, but no systematic homogeneity measurement exists.

Chain of Attack shows adversarial transferability across VLMs but does not measure semantic homogeneity of normal outputs. This is a genuinely unexplored extension.
